title: Using the Pit
description: The app, taught the way the app teaches everything else.

cards.front: What happens to a card you get right?
cards.back: It comes back later — a day, then three, then further each time
cards.note: Spacing the reviews out just before you forget is the whole engine.

cards.front: What happens to a card you get wrong?
cards.back: It comes back inside the same sitting

cards.front: What does ⏻ park it do to a card?
cards.back: Takes it out of rotation until you let it back in
cards.note: From the editor, Resume gives it a clean slate.

cards.front: What is ★ star it for?
cards.back: Marking a card to come back to, whatever the schedule thinks
cards.note: The home screen collects starred cards into one drill.

cards.front: What does a card parked by itself after eight misses mean?
cards.back: The card is wrong, not you — rewrite it
cards.note: A card that asks two things, or gives itself away, fails like this.

cards.front: Why does the exam mode not touch your streak?
cards.back: An exam measures; only practice trains

cards.front: Where does a note you add after missing a card show up?
cards.back: Under the answer, every time you answer that card

cards.front: What does mixing two modules into one sitting do for you?
cards.back: Interleaving — harder in the moment, better remembered
cards.note: The Learning Science module has the study behind this.

cards.front: What is the fastest way to add one fact you just learned?
cards.back: Quick card, on the home screen

cards.front: How do you turn a Claude answer into a module?
cards.back: Paste it into Import — tables, Q&A lines and lists all work
cards.note: A paste with several ## headings becomes several modules.

cards.front: What earns the certificate on a module?
cards.back: Every card resting at once

cards.front: What breaks a streak?
cards.back: Missing two days — one is forgiven once a week
cards.note: A rest day exists so a busy Tuesday doesn't erase a habit.

cards.front: What happens when you mix the same two cards up twice?
cards.back: They appear on progress as Often confused, with a pair drill one tap away
cards.note: One mix-up is noise; the same pair again is a diagnosis.

cards.front: What does 'Spread it over the week' do to a huge due pile?
cards.back: Deals it out evenly over seven days, oldest first
cards.note: The returned-from-holiday button. Undo puts every card back.

cards.front: Where do the cards you missed go after a sitting?
cards.back: Into a one-tap drill, or to Claude as a brief for sharper cards
cards.note: A card missed repeatedly is usually the card's fault — rewrite it.

cards.front: How do you get reminded to study without the app nagging you?
cards.back: Settings makes a daily calendar event — the calendar does the reminding

cards.front: What does ⏾ not today do to a card?
cards.back: Puts it off until tomorrow, ungraded
cards.note: Between skip (back later this sitting) and park (gone until you say).

cards.front: How does the Ladder decide how to ask each card?
cards.back: By how well you know it — new among options, young with a blank, old from nothing
cards.note: A miss drops the card back to the first rung. Review due on the home screen is a Ladder.

cards.front: What does a card need before Order it will deal it?
cards.back: An answer that is a sequence — steps joined by → or ;

cards.front: What do the small words under Again, Good and Easy tell you?
cards.back: When the card would come back if you pressed that one

cards.front: What does 'Wrong in a flash' on the results screen mean?
cards.back: You missed it too fast to have tried — a guess, not an attempt
cards.note: The attempt to retrieve is where the learning happens, even when it fails.

cards.front: What changes in the last three days before a deadline?
cards.back: Every card you have seen is asked once more, soonest due first

cards.front: What does Say it do with a language module?
cards.back: Says the answer properly, listens to you say it, and shows which words came out

cards.front: A card has no hint. What does asking for one show?
cards.back: The shape of the answer — first letter, then blanks

cards.front: No picture for a card? What does Find one do?
cards.back: Searches Wikimedia Commons and keeps the picture's page as the source
